svg.text: FRCS Part 1 (General Surgery) · sheet 1 of 2 · pleomorphic · Warthin's · mucoepidermoid · adenoid cystic · the 80% rule
~80% of salivary tumours arise in the parotid; ~80% of parotid tumours are benign; ~80% of those are pleomorphic adenomas —
and ~80% sit in the superficial lobe.
few tumours, but the majority are malignant
The smaller the gland, the higher the chance a tumour is malignant.
Mixed — epithelial + myoepithelial cells in a chondromyxoid stroma
Pseudopod extensions breach the capsule → recurs if enucleated
Carcinoma ex-pleomorphic adenoma with time → excise, don't watch
Older male smokers; the ONLY bilateral / multifocal tumour (~10%)
Oncocytic epithelium on a lymphoid stroma; cystic
Mucous + epidermoid cells; graded low → high
Indolent but relentless; late lung metastases;
Malignant change in a long-standing pleomorphic
MALT lymphoma on a background of Sjögren's
Do NOT perform an incisional / open biopsy of a parotid mass — it risks tumour seeding and facial-nerve injury. Use image-guided
Never enucleate a pleomorphic adenoma — microscopic pseudopods breach the capsule, so incomplete excision recurs; do a
A facial-nerve palsy with a parotid mass means malignancy until proven otherwise — benign tumours do not paralyse the
Adenoid cystic carcinoma looks indolent but tracks perineurally and relapses with lung metastases years later — it needs long
Warthin's is the bilateral / multifocal tumour of older male smokers, and it lights up on technetium scanning.
The smaller the salivary gland, the higher the chance a tumour is malignant — parotid least, minor glands most.
Sources: Management of Salivary Gland Tumours — UK National Multidisciplinary Guidelines (2016) · Royal College of Pathologists salivary dataset · WHO classification of head & neck
tumours · standard head & neck surgical texts.
